title: Marguerite and the Echo
premise: Lior Crane, a clone of a murdered courier, inherits both her original's route and her unsolved case. When the name 'Marguerite' appears on the manifest of a ship that was decommissioned before Lior was decanted, she follows it into the silence between two warring colonies and discovers her original was carrying proof that one side manufactured the war. The message Marguerite left can end the conflict — but delivering it means exposing Lior's own illegal existence, since clones are contraband in both systems. In the end, Lior broadcasts the truth from inside the derelict ship, choosing to be seen over staying safe, and survives as the first clone to be legally recognized — at the cost of everything she had built to stay invisible.
about_author: S. M. Dunmore is the pen name of a former shipping-logistics analyst who spent a decade writing about cargo that never quite matched its manifests. They live near a decommissioned spaceport and write stories about people who carry things they were never meant to open.

chapters.title: The Long Route
chapters.summary: Lior runs her courier loop between the silent colonies of Vesper and Calloway, establishing her careful, invisible life. POV: Lior. Emotional beat: competent loneliness — she's good at her job precisely because no one looks at her.

chapters.title: Inheritance
chapters.summary: Flashback woven through present: Lior was decanted after her original's murder, inheriting her contracts, debts, and an unsolved case file she's forbidden to open. POV: Lior. Emotional beat: grief worn as routine; she is living someone else's unfinished sentence.

chapters.title: A Name That Shouldn't Exist
chapters.summary: Auditing old manifests to renew her license, Lior finds 'Marguerite' listed on the Halcyon Dawn — a ship scrapped eleven years before Lior was decanted. POV: Lior. Emotional beat: the first crack in her invisibility; curiosity overriding fear.

chapters.title: Questions at the Dock
chapters.summary: Lior quietly asks around the dockyards and learns someone else has been asking the same question — and that askers tend to disappear. POV: Lior. Emotional beat: dread arriving ahead of danger.

chapters.title: The Tail
chapters.summary: A gray-cloaked stranger follows Lior through Vesper's underlevels; she loses them using courier routes only her original would have known. POV: Lior. Emotional beat: realization that her original's habits are a map someone else can read.

chapters.title: Calloway Side
chapters.summary: On the enemy colony, Lior meets Idris Vale, a records clerk who owes her original a favor and confirms Marguerite was a person, not cargo: a negotiator who vanished mid-peace-talks. POV: Lior. Emotional beat: the war acquires a human face.

chapters.title: What the Original Knew
chapters.summary: Idris shares fragments of the original Crane's investigation: evidence the blockade that started the war was staged by Vesper's own ruling consortium. POV: alternating Lior/Idris. Emotional beat: vertigo — the enemy side holds more of her own history than she does.

chapters.title: Burn Notice
chapters.summary: Lior's docking privileges are revoked without explanation; someone with authority wants her grounded. POV: Lior. Emotional beat: the trap closing — invisibility failing exactly when she needs it most.

chapters.title: The Gray Cloak Speaks
chapters.summary: Cornered, Lior confronts her tail: Sef Andrade, a consortium fixer who claims he's trying to keep the message buried for everyone's good. POV: Lior/Sef. Emotional beat: a villain who sounds reasonable — power justifying itself.

chapters.title: Marguerite's Vault
chapters.summary: Following coordinates hidden in her original's case file, Lior reaches the Halcyon Dawn's hulk drifting in dead space and finds Marguerite alive in cryo — barely. POV: Lior. Emotional beat: awe and terror; the ghost becomes a witness.

chapters.title: The Message
chapters.summary: Revived just enough to speak, Marguerite reveals she hid full proof of the staged blockade aboard the ship and encoded its location in a phrase only a Crane could unlock. POV: Marguerite. Emotional beat: the weight of memory — a woman who chose to be forgotten so the truth would survive.

chapters.title: Unlocking
chapters.summary: Lior deciphers the lock using memories that are hers only by inheritance, forcing her to accept her original's life as genuinely her own. POV: Lior. Emotional beat: identity resolved not as copy versus original, but as continuation.

chapters.title: Sef's Offer
chapters.summary: Andrade boards the hulk and offers Lior citizenship, wealth, legal humanity — if she hands over the proof and lets the war grind on. POV: Lior. Emotional beat: temptation articulated perfectly; survival priced against justice.

chapters.title: Refusal
chapters.summary: Lior refuses; Sef takes Marguerite and scuttles toward the hulk's reactor, leaving Lior to die with the ship. POV: Lior. Emotional beat: betrayal crystallizing into resolve.

chapters.title: Dead Space Run
chapters.summary: Liar repairs the Halcyon Dawn's ancient drive using skills from two lifetimes and limps back toward inhabited space, pursued. POV: Lior. Emotional beat: ferocious competence — the invisible woman becoming unstoppable.

chapters.title: Two Fleets
chapters.summary: She arrives to find Vesper and Calloway fleets on the brink of final battle over the debris field where the 'attack' happened. POV: multiple fleet officers briefly, then Lior. Emotional beat: scale — individual truth against institutional momentum.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Lior seizes the relay array and transmits the full proof — including her own clone status, burning her last protection. POV: Lior. Emotional beat: climax; the price paid willingly, in public.

chapters.title: The Fleet That Stopped
chapters.summary: Weapons hold as the evidence spreads through both fleets; crews refuse the order to fire. Sef Andrade is arrested by his own consortium. POV: ensemble. Emotional beat: catharsis — power's machinery jammed by truth.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Marguerite, recovering, testifies at the joint tribunal; Lior watches the war formally end and the clone prohibition collapse under scrutiny of what she did. POV: Lior/Marguerite. Emotional beat: quiet vindication.

chapters.title: Recognition
chapters.summary: Lior is offered honors and a new identity; instead she asks for her original's name cleared and her own kept small. POV: Lior. Emotional beat: choosing visibility on her own terms rather than fame.

chapters.title: Echo
chapters.summary: Lior visits her original's grave and finally reads the unsolved case file cover to cover — closed now, solved by her. POV: Lior. Emotional beat: mourning completed; inheritance accepted.

chapters.title: The Long Route, Again
chapters.summary: Lior reopens the courier run between worlds that now speak, carrying ordinary mail and, once, a letter from Marguerite. POV: Lior. Emotional beat: peace earned — the same road, a different woman walking it.
